exposure: Mode of first delivery (cesarean or vaginal)
cohort: 2423 women aged 18 to 35 years with singleton pregnancies who delivered in Pennsylvania from 2009 to 2011
finding: Women who had a cesarean delivery for their first child had lower rates of conception and subsequent live births within 3 years compared to women who delivered vaginally.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with lower rates of conception after unprotected intercourse and fewer subsequent live births compared to vaginal delivery.
